title: ʻOkina & Kahakō
description: Train your eye and keyboard to treat Hawaiian orthography as part of the word itself.

activities.support: Add the Hawaiian orthography that is missing.
activities.explanation: ʻAʻole begins with an ʻokina and the o carries a kahakō. Both marks affect how the word is pronounced.

activities.support: Type the place name using the Hawaiian ʻokina.
activities.explanation: The ʻokina in Hawaiʻi represents a glottal stop; it is a letter/sound in Hawaiian orthography, not decoration.

activities.support: Restore the missing ʻokina and kahakō.
activities.explanation: ʻŌlelo begins with an ʻokina and a long ō. Hawaiʻi also contains an ʻokina.

activities.support: This short word still needs its initial consonant.
activities.explanation: The initial ʻokina is pronounced as a glottal stop. Short words are not exempt from Hawaiian orthography.

activities.instruction: Type this exactly from memory after looking away for a moment.
activities.support: Focus on where the ʻokina and kahakō belong.
activities.explanation: Accurate copying helps turn the ʻokina and kahakō into automatic spelling habits rather than optional marks.
